entries.action: Cite as the body-class verdict: permutation-invariant attention loses temporal order; linear-first doctrine stands. Any body variant opens with a ridge baseline (P1 gate).
entries.note: permutation-invariant self-attention loses temporal order; embarrassingly simple one-layer LTSF-Linear beats transformer LTSF models on all nine datasets, often by margin. Converges with B2 (ridge 2x transformer on big-move), m5g (raw +0.18 vs members -0.05), 2605.05151 (narrow single-layer matches deep stacks).

entries.title: Are Transformers Effective for Time Series Forecasting?

entries.action: Design-only body variant R-BODY-1 (behind P1): one token per indicator-channel, attention over variates, FFN per variate; killer = P1 stacking-gate.
entries.note: repurposes transformer without component change: time points of each series embedded as variate tokens, attention captures multivariate correlations, FFN learns per-variate nonlinearities. SOTA with better lookback use and cross-variate generalization. Maps onto our S1/S2 directly: today 10 indicators are fused then mean-pooled; inverted form keeps each channel a token to the readout.
entries.relevance: body replacement candidate R-BODY-1 (variate-token member): preserves the hivemind shell, changes only what attention mixes.
entries.title: iTransformer: Inverted Transformers Are Effective for Time Series Forecasting

entries.action: Design-only body variant R-BODY-2 (behind P1): patch-window + channel-independent member, shared weights per channel; killer = P1 stacking-gate.
entries.note: patch segmentation (local semantics, quadratic attention saving, longer history) + channel-independence (one univariate series per channel, shared embedding/weights). Significant long-term accuracy gains. Maps onto S2 window handling: patch the feature window instead of attending raw bars; share weights across indicator channels.
entries.relevance: body replacement candidate R-BODY-2 (patch + channel-independent member).
entries.title: A Time Series is Worth 64 Words: Long-term Forecasting with Transformers

entries.action: Run P2 as validation-chosen transforms: detrended/differenced/raw variants per indicator; never blanket-squash. Killer: no variant beats stock on skill.
entries.note: 35,099-eval controlled study (18 synthetic DGPs x 10 transforms x 5 models x 3 horizons + 9 real series): signal-preserving transforms (deterministic detrending, structure-matched seasonal differencing) help; indiscriminate differencing hurts; trend-stationarity only weakly tied to accuracy; validation-chosen transform beats unit-root pretests and fixed rules; blanket differencing worst. Re-verified abstract this cycle.

entries.action: Hold the body verdict closed: no superposition hunt, no depth scaling on this data.
entries.note: SAE probes on PatchTST FFN reps: narrow single-layer matches deep configs; 0.5x-4x dictionary expansion moves performance 0.214% avg with dead latents; causal interventions perturb little. No superposition; benchmarks do not demand compositional reps; explains linear competitiveness. Re-verified abstract; converges with B2/m5g. Re-verified abstract this cycle.
